notes:
• Pocket shows changes on the Mac right away: new messages, a chat's state, the workspace list and the pull request bar update about 0.2 s after Conductor writes them, instead of on a 1.5–6 s timer. Pocket Host learns about changes from the operating system (writes to Conductor's database and git caches) and streams them to the phone. Notifications go out sooner too. With an older Pocket Host the apps keep polling as before.
• Pocket Host has a "Name on the phone" field to give the Mac a name of its own instead of the computer name (which macOS sometimes numbers, like "MacBook Pro (1021)"). The apps pick up a new name the next time the workspace list or Settings opens, without pairing again.
• Tapping a workspace in the list loads its chat before it opens: a spinner shows on the row (in place of the chevron on iPhone, of the time on Android) and the chat comes up already filled in. If the Mac takes longer than a few seconds, the chat opens anyway and finishes loading there.
• Sending from the phone no longer fails with "Conductor has no open window": Pocket Host brings Conductor's window back (closed, minimized or hidden), and starts Conductor first when it isn't running.
• Tapping a notification while a chat is open now opens the notification's chat, also in another workspace, instead of only changing the title.
• iPhone: swiping back from a chat to the workspaces slides the chat's title along smoothly instead of making it wobble.
